purpose: Define deterministic, lossless, bidirectional lookup indexes derived only from the B-4 validated Hero <-> Exclusive Equipment canonical relation.

publicationGate.requiredRelationBlobSha: The exact gitBlobSha pinned by B-4 validation.
publicationGate.rule: B-5 must abort if the current relation blob SHA differs from the blob SHA validated by B-4.

authority.rule: Indexes may only project existing canonical pairs. They may not add, remove, repair, reinterpret, infer, or override ownership.

byHero.entryRule: Create keys only for Hero IDs present in canonical relation edges.
byHero.missingKeyMeaning: This Hero has no current canonical exclusive-equipment ownership edge in this relation snapshot; it does not mean the Hero ID is invalid.

byEquipment.entryRule: Create keys only for Equipment IDs present in canonical relation edges.
byEquipment.missingKeyMeaning: This Equipment ID has no canonical Stage B ownership edge; B-4 requires every frozen exclusive Equipment ID to be present.

generationAlgorithm: Read B-4 validation and require PASS / COMPLETE.
Compute the current Git blob SHA of data/generated/hero-exclusive-equipment-relations.v1.json and require exact equality with B-4 relationSet.gitBlobSha.
Read only canonical relation records as semantic membership input.
For each canonical edge (heroId, equipmentId), append equipmentId to byHeroId[String(heroId)] and append heroId to byEquipmentId[String(equipmentId)].
Do not derive one index from the other.
Sort numeric keys ascending and sort every value array ascending.
Write both indexes referencing the exact same canonical relation blob SHA.
Validate both reconstructed pair sets independently against the canonical pair set before publication.

cardinalityProjection.shapePolicy: Values remain arrays even while B-4 cardinality is zero-or-one / exactly-one so consumer structure does not depend on a scalar optimization.

ordering.determinism: Identical canonical relation content must yield semantically identical index maps independent of source record iteration order.

relationSet.gitBlobSha: Exact B-4 validated relation blob SHA

summary.relationCount: Sum of all value array lengths

parityInvariants: Both index artifacts reference the same exact B-4 validated relation blob SHA.
byHero relationCount equals canonical edge count 167.
byEquipment relationCount equals canonical edge count 167.
byHero keyCount equals distinct heroId count in canonical edges: 167.
byEquipment keyCount equals distinct equipmentId count in canonical edges: 167.
Every canonical pair appears exactly once in each directional reconstruction.
No pair absent from canonical edges appears in either index.
Pair set reconstructed from byHeroId exactly equals the canonical pair set.
Pair set reconstructed from byEquipmentId exactly equals the canonical pair set.
Both reconstructed pair sets exactly equal one another.

consumerBoundary.heroStage5_2: Consume byHeroId to locate exclusive equipment IDs, then join display payload by equipmentId. Do not reopen ConfigData ownership logic.
consumerBoundary.equipmentPage: Consume byEquipmentId to locate owner Hero IDs, then join canonical Hero metadata. Do not infer owner from names, restrictions, ordering, or other equipment metadata.
consumerBoundary.generalEquipment: General Equipment remains outside Stage B and must not appear in either index.

failurePolicy: If B-4 validation is not PASS / COMPLETE, do not generate B-5 indexes.
If relation blob SHA differs from B-4, stop and require B-4 revalidation.
If either index parity check fails, discard/regenerate indexes; never alter canonical edges to make an index pass.
Do not silently deduplicate malformed canonical pairs or duplicate index values.
Do not repair one index from the other index or from ConfigData.
completion: B-5 is complete when byHero and byEquipment are generated only from the exact B-4 validated relation blob, both directions contain 167 relations with frozen cardinality preserved, and independent round-trip reconstruction yields zero pair mismatch and zero hard errors.
